$comment: The source of sf-editor-overlay's interface (core/js/element-manifest.js over core/js/composition/manifest-host.mjs). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/composition-overlay (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

for.summary: The id of the canvas element the overlay draws over

frame.summary: The id of a same-origin iframe canvas (framed mode, fed by setNodes)

accepts.summary: sf-sortable groups whose items may be dropped on the canvas, separated by spaces

label.summary: The structure tree's name; the language file's runtime.tree otherwise

placement.summary: Where the toolbar stands: top, above the block and right-aligned, the default; side, beside the block on a host with room beside it, above the block where there is none

passive.summary: Takes no input on the canvas while on: clicks, double clicks, keys, hover and drops reach the page (an editor the host placed in a chosen block), the selection is kept and the selected frame stays drawn; the toolbar, insertion points and move handle step aside and the tree leaves the Tab order. Off again, the overlay reads input as before

actions.summary: The selected node's actions: up to 16 {id, label} with optional icon, shortcut, disabled and tone; written through the same check as setActions

messages.summary: The host's own words over the language file's; written through setMessages

insertion-target.summary: The insertion place the host keeps marked {parent_id, slot, index}; written through setInsertionTarget

node_id.summary: The selected node id, null when the selection cleared; kept for the composition host (the Document mode reads it)

select.summary: A node was selected (or the selection cleared): vocabulary 1.1.5 §5 select; the detail keeps node_id for the composition host

apply.summary: An action of the toolbar was chosen for the selected node: one entry's own action (vocabulary §5 apply, standard §18.3)

parent_id.summary: The parent node of the place; kept for the composition host (the Document mode reads it)

insert.summary: An insertion point was chosen, or a library item dropped on the canvas: the place {parent, slot, index} and the item when one was dragged; the detail keeps parent_id for the composition host

node_id.summary: The moved node; kept for the composition host (the Document mode reads it)

parent_id.summary: The new parent node; kept for the composition host (the Document mode reads it)

index.summary: The place among the parent slot children; kept for the composition host (the Document mode reads it)

move.summary: A node was moved to a place by pointer or keyboard: one manual move (vocabulary §5 move, {id, parent, position}); the detail keeps node_id, parent_id and index for the composition host

change.summary: A plain-string edit was committed; cancelled, the text shows what it showed before

node.summary: The node to open; the same id as id

point.summary: {x, y} in canvas coordinates: from the canvas element's border box corner, or a framed canvas's viewport (the frame document's client coordinates); the pointer for a click or a double click, the centre of the node's box for Enter; null when it cannot be measured

trigger.summary: What asked: a second click on the chosen node, a double click, or Enter in the tree

open.summary: The person asked to open a node: a second click on the chosen node, a double click on a node, or Enter on the chosen node in the tree (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5 open). Sent once per gesture and never while passive; an editable node of a framed canvas opens by its own plain-string edit instead

attach.summary: Draws over a canvas element; the canvas is never modified

attach-frame.summary: Draws over a same-origin iframe canvas fed by set-nodes

set-nodes.summary: Reads a flat node list (framed mode)

filter.summary: A function (place, item) => boolean; place is {parent_id, slot, index}

set-drop-filter.summary: filter({parent_id, slot, index}, item) hides the places a drop may not take

set-actions.summary: Writes the selected node's actions (the actions setting)

set-messages.summary: Writes the host's own words (the messages setting)

set-insertion-target.summary: Writes the marked insertion place (the insertion-target setting)

edit.summary: Starts a plain-string edit of an editable node

default.$comment: The overlay draws its frames, toolbar, insertion points and structure tree itself (core/js/composition/overlay.mjs); the canvas is the host's and is never changed.

accessibility.$comment: The structure tree is the overlay's keyboard surface: role tree, named by label (the language file's «Структура страницы» otherwise), one Tab stop; the arrows walk the nodes, Enter or Space selects (Enter on the chosen node also sends open), Escape closes a move or an edit; the toolbar is role toolbar; each step is said in a polite live region.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-editor-overlay for the shim (stands/18-aliases-ci/alias.mjs, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), split / detail-adds (a detail adapter, refused by the shim), attribute-and-property, method, property, manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), host-attribute (no shim), retired.

rows.summary: Dated alias of sf-composition-overlay-apply until 2026-12-01: A toolbar action was chosen.

rows.summary: Dated alias of sf-composition-overlay-change until 2026-12-01: A plain-string inline edit was committed with a changed value (framed mode). Cancelable: preventDefault puts the previous text back.

x-summary: The editor's layer over a rendered Composition Document: hover and selection frames, a toolbar of the node's actions, insertion places, moves by pointer and keyboard and a structure tree; the canvas is never changed and the host performs every change.
x-renamed: events.sf-composition-overlay-action {action_id, node_id} → apply {action, scope: entry, ids}: one entry's own action (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5 apply, standard §18.3); sf-composition-overlay-apply, the old name a dated split alias

events.sf-composition-overlay-edit {node_id, value, previous} → change {id, value, previous}, cancelable: a committed value (vocabulary §5.1, as sf-inline-edit-commit and sf-theme-change); sf-composition-overlay-change, the old name a dated split alias sharing the cancel
events select and move keep their DOM names (vocabulary §5 select, move) and add the vocabulary's fields (ids, id; ids, id, parent, position) beside node_id, parent_id and index
methods setActions, setMessages, setInsertionTarget: also the settings actions, messages and insertion-target (properties)
lang runtime holds the words of the overlay module (MESSAGES of core/js/composition/overlay.mjs)
x-decisions: events (vocabulary 1.1.5): select {ids, id}, apply {action, scope: entry, ids} for the toolbar's action, insert (the component's own verb: a place chosen or a library item dropped -- a move or a copy, not §5 create), move {ids, id, parent, position} -- one manual move -- and change {id, value, previous}, cancelable, for a plain-string edit (x-native false: sf-composition-overlay-change).

the composition host's contract stays (larena composition-editor-next listens to -select, -action, -move and -insert): select, move and insert keep their DOM names and keep node_id, parent_id and index in the detail beside the vocabulary's fields; action and edit are followed by sf-composition-overlay-action {action_id, node_id} and -edit {node_id, value, previous} until 2026-12-01 through the overlay's aliases.json and the element's adapters, the cancel of the edit shared. An overlay defined without its manifest sends both itself. OVERLAY_EVENTS holds the new names, OVERLAY_EVENTS_LEGACY the former.
own-verb-words: insert -- its word is events.insert.label of the language files («Вставить», "Insert"); action became apply, edit became change.
setter: actions, messages and insertion-target are writable settings, properties written through the same checks as setActions, setMessages and setInsertionTarget, which stay the host's port.

the methods attach, attach-frame, set-document, set-nodes, set-drop-filter, set-actions, set-messages, set-insertion-target, select, edit and refresh are the composition host's port (simai.composition editor): they keep answering the element, for chaining, not an outcome (x-returns); the port stays as the composition editor uses it.
item-shape: actions name their fields with of ({id, label}, checkOverlayActions); set-nodes takes a list of nodes {id, kind, label, parent, editable, rect | element} (checkOverlayNodes).

element: the overlay stays the plain element the composition module defines; defineCompositionOverlay(registry, {base}) extends the class core/js/composition/manifest-host.mjs makes from this component.json (the settings' properties, the aliases.json shim, sfWord).
words (§11): the language files hold the overlay module's words; the module keeps its copy and reads them through the page's language; messages overrides them per instance.
version 1.2.0: events renamed behind dated aliases and detail fields added (§4.10).
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (an overlay for a canvas) plus a framed canvas, a library that drops on the canvas and actions.

css-variables: five public variables of its sheet: the frames' and insertion points' colour (read into the overlay's own --sf-composition-overlay-color), the layer's z-index, the toolbar's fill, radius and gap. Not in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json: the parts they colour exist only over a canvas with a selection, which its probe does not draw.

source-drift: the shipped manifest differs from 5100227 in the framed mode (frame, attach-frame, set-nodes, simai/ui-source#22) and the plain-string edit (sf-composition-overlay-edit); they are carried here by hand.

version 1.2.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.

version 1.2.2: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

version 1.3.0, owner's decision of 2026-10-31 on selecting, moving and adding a block: actions carry optional icon, shortcut, disabled and tone; the setting placement (top, side); hover and selection are bare frames of 1px and 2px; one insertion point at the seam under the pointer; moves glide 180 ms; dragging by the action whose icon is drag_indicator; an overlay in the scroller of its canvas lives in the scrolled content and runs nothing on scroll.

version 1.4.0: the tag is sf-editor-overlay (naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>[-<variant>]); the folder, the id smart.editor-overlay and the bundle cl-editor-overlay follow it. sf-composition-overlay stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: a subclass the Smart base defines beside the new tag, listed in the rule, in sheets as :is(sf-editor-overlay, sf-composition-overlay) (change journal tag-sf-composition-overlay-to-sf-editor-overlay, path-smart-composition-overlay-to-editor-overlay).

version 1.5.0 (ui-editor gaps G-16 and G-17, 2026-11-05): the setting passive (boolean, default off) -- the overlay takes no input on its canvas while on: no click, double click, key, hover, seam or drop is read, prevented or stopped, so an editor the host placed in a chosen block gets them; the node list and the selection are kept, the selected frame stays drawn, the toolbar, insertion points and move handle step aside and the tree leaves the Tab order; an inline edit in progress commits, a move cancels. The event open {ids, id, node, point, trigger} (vocabulary §5 open, DOM sf-editor-overlay-open, sent under the former tag as sf-composition-overlay-open until 2027-01-01 like every event named after the tag): a second click on the chosen node (trigger click), a double click on a node (dblclick; it selects the node first), or Enter on the chosen node in the tree (enter; the toolbar still takes the focus, a host that opens takes it from there). point is in canvas coordinates -- from the canvas element's border box corner, or a framed canvas's viewport -- the pointer for a click, the centre of the node's box for Enter. One open per gesture: the double click a first click began opens nothing more. An editable node of a framed canvas keeps its own plain-string edit on double click and Enter and sends no open. Both are additions: a host that sets neither sees 1.4.0's behaviour.

version 1.5.1 (simai/ui-source#62, 2026-11-08): after a pointer selection on a 'for' canvas the selected node's action shortcuts are taken where the click left focus -- on the canvas or an element in it that types no text, or on an element holding the canvas (its scroller, the body) -- as a framed canvas takes them inside its frame. Only the shortcuts: a text field or an editable in a block, the tree and the toolbar keep their keys, a key already prevented is left alone, nothing is read while passive, and of several overlays the one clicked last takes them. Focus does not move, so a click draws no focus outline.
version 1.5.2: its embedded sortable primitive gives the instructions a page-wide counted id (sf-sortable 1.1.8, core.runtime 1.38.0); nothing else changed.

canvas.description: The canvas holds host-rendered Composition HTML with data-sf-composition-id; the overlay never writes into it, so published HTML and digests are identical with the editor open or closed. Place the overlay before the canvas, inside the scroller that scrolls it: its tree comes first in Tab order and its parts travel with the content.

browser_api.description: Once loaded, SF.CompositionOverlay exposes OVERLAY_EVENTS, overlayNodes(document), checkOverlayActions(actions) and checkOverlayNodes(nodes).

frame_canvas.description: Framed mode: the canvas is a same-origin iframe (sandbox allow-same-origin is enough; the frame needs no script). The overlay reads the frame's document, listens to its pointer, key, scroll and resize events and maps frame coordinates to the host through the iframe's position, border, padding, transform or zoom and the frame's scroll. It writes nothing into the frame except a temporary contenteditable on the element being edited. A frame that reloads (srcdoc) is listened to again on load; the host then calls setNodes with the new document's elements.

nodes.description: Framed mode's flat node list, in selection order. element is a node inside the frame document; rect is in frame-document coordinates (viewport box plus the frame's scroll). parent names another node of the list (siblings share a parent; the top level has none). editable allows plain-string inline editing of the element.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-composition-overlay on an editor page over SF.Composition.render output. Treat every event as intent: the host changes the Document, saves it with an expected revision, validates and re-renders. For a canvas isolated in a same-origin iframe (a mail letter), use attachFrame (or frame="id") and setNodes with a flat node list; edits arrive as sf-composition-overlay-edit.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not write editor markup into the canvas HTML
Do not treat setDropFilter as validation; Document validation stays authoritative
Do not put the overlay after the canvas in Tab order
Do not expect the overlay to keep an edited text: it raises the intent, the host updates its model and re-renders the frame
Do not point the framed mode at a cross-origin frame

accessibility.focus: The tree has one treeitem per node; arrows move in document order and between parent and child, Enter opens the toolbar and sends open for the chosen node, Escape returns or clears. Space starts a keyboard move, arrows choose a place, Enter drops, Escape cancels. Selection and moves are announced. In framed mode the tree follows the node list order, pointer and keys inside the frame select too, Enter on an editable node starts plain-text editing in the frame (Enter commits, Escape cancels, focus returns to the tree), and Escape gives way to an inner open surface. While passive the tree is out of the Tab order and reads no key.

sf-composition-overlay-action.summary: Dated alias of sf-composition-overlay-apply until 2026-12-01: A toolbar action was chosen. Its detail is the former one, {action_id, node_id}, not sf-composition-overlay-apply's {action, scope, ids}.

sf-composition-overlay-edit.summary: Dated alias of sf-composition-overlay-change until 2026-12-01: A plain-string inline edit was committed with a changed value (framed mode). Cancelable: preventDefault puts the previous text back. Its detail is the former one, {node_id, value, previous}, not sf-composition-overlay-change's {id, value, previous}.
